sm_github.json:97:          "description": "gh-807 VERDICT RECONCILIATION, shape 3 of 3: a sticky pr_approved whose newest verdict for the CURRENT head is REQUEST_CHANGES/BLOCK — the approval is stale, approval-gated paths are blocked until re-review, and the label comes off the PR (pr_approved never lives on the issue; the action still posts the one both-sources comment, AC2). NOT gated on the arm-preserving exemptions (a checksRed red or a blocking>0 census keep agent:rework, never the approval): red CI never legitimizes an approval. Runs before the merge window every tick so merge-validated/validate-armed (which also carry notLatestVerdict as belt-and-suspenders for the same tick) see reconciled labels; the notLatestVerdict lanes make this rule's work mostly convergent the moment it fires. PRs without verdict records fail open (pre-gh-807 behavior).",
sm_github.json:114:          "description": "Validated-but-stale: armed (ai_validating) + validation concluded but BASE MOVED (BEHIND only). BLOCKED must NOT unarm: since #483 BLOCKED is a real verdict, and on a freshly armed head BLOCKED simply means 'required checks pending' — unarming there races validate-armed in the SAME tick and deadlocks the PR forever (live: fa pr-762 armed at 08:25:37, unarmed 08:25:58 by the BLOCKED match, re-armed next tick, loop). silent-update-behind excludes ai_validating and merge-validated needs CLEAN, so without this unarm a genuinely moved base still deadlocks (live: fa pr-744) — BEHIND-only keeps that recovery and stops the self-inflicted one. gh-751 VERDICT-AWARE STRIP (live: fa #1295 — the arm was stripped FIVE times in one day with zero latches, [ai_validating]→[]→[ai_validating] yo-yo under a saturated CI queue): every main merge made the armed head BEHIND and this strip DISCARDED the head's ALREADY-CONCLUDED green verdict — it lost the race to the strip (merge-validated needs CLEAN; validated-green sits later and excludes pr_approved), silent-update refreshed, validate-fresh re-armed, the next merge re-struck: a full re-validation per main merge. The action now probes the head's dispatched validation runs before stripping: a GREEN run ANYWHERE on the head latches ai_validated instead of the bare unarm — not only the newest run: gh-748 showed two workflow_dispatch runs landing on ONE head seconds apart, and the latch consumer (validate-armed's skipIfValidatedHead → hasSuccessfulDispatchedRun) accepts any completed-green run on the head, so the strip consumes that same facet (complete_validation parity — sweep_stale_validation's success-branch shape; the latch excludes the PR from validate-fresh, and validate-armed latch-skips on the unchanged head so the merge window re-flows without new CI); only when NO green run exists on the head (red / absent / in-flight / cancelled-only) does the bare unarm stand (refresh + re-validate recovery).",
sm_github.json:131:          "description": "RULE ORDER (dmtools-agents#637 aftermath, live fa pr-1174 2026-10-03): this rule MUST run before sweep-stale-validating — the 15-min staleness sweep eats every arm before the merge can consume it whenever the tick cadence slips past 15 min (night kicker slippage), looping arm→sweep→arm on a green merge-ready head. GitHub PR: validation green + CLEAN -> squash-merge (merge_pr verifies the sticky pr_approved latch on the PR; an un-approved green head latches ai_validated instead — see merge_pr). FIFO drain (#687). PRIORITY TIERS (owner directive 2026-10-08, amends the 2026-09-22 FIFO rule): the merge pick is FIFO WITHIN a tier — a priority_blocker merges FIRST, ahead of older mediums (this limit-1 pick shares validate-armed's tier-aware sort in queryPrs; a preemption logs a 🥇 line in the tick log), priority_low SINKS below all mediums, and a PR with NO priority label is medium (the priority_medium label is NOT required to exist). Carrier: the label may sit on the PR OR its linked issue — either counts. Label NAMES configurable per project via .dmtools/config.js smPriorityLabels (defaults blocker/medium/low = priority_blocker/priority_medium/priority_low; absent mapping entries degrade to the defaults).",
sm_github.json:150:          "description": "RULE ORDER (owner directive 2026-10-04 'red yields the slot', live fa 11:0x: #1194 held ai_validating through repeated reds while #1215..#1223 sat FIFO-queued 40+ min): this rule MUST run BEFORE validate-armed — the unarm below frees the limit-1 mutex and (with the openPrs ioCache drop in the action) the arm rule's later query in the SAME tick sees the freed slot and arms the NEXT oldest approved PR immediately. Previously fail-validation ran after validate-armed: the arm rule scanned the still-occupied mutex every tick and the slot stayed hostage until the failed PR's rework cycle re-armed it. #637 rule-order invariant preserved: rerun-cancelled-checks stays first (#682/gh-682), and merge-validated still runs before sweep-stale-validating. GitHub PR: validation CI red on the head -> unarm ai_validating, report (with the 🔴 red-head counter marker — the validate_pr arm side skips heads with >= redHeadCap recorded reds), requeue agent:rework on the linked issue. pr_approved is STICKY (owner rule 2026-09): the reworked head re-validates and merges without a re-review — no token burn on review legs. GUEST PRs (gh-757, live fa#1286: the 2026-10-04 guest validation-red arm spent an AI rework leg on a vendor PR): report + validation_failed PARK only — auto-rework is machine-author-ONLY (owner rule 2026-09-21 reaffirmed); the guest's own push clears the park (#633 RESET) and validation re-runs, and a HUMAN can still arm agent:rework manually on any PR (rework-on-label). Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): latch/unlatch verdicts in waves — pure label writes, nothing serial. gh-832 CONVERGENCE PARK (live fa #1453, 2026-10-10: 12 dispatch→red→unarm→rearm cycles on an unchanged approved head, 5 reds in a row, window idle 3.5h, no park, no comment): repeated red verdicts must never loop — the fail path counts CONSECUTIVE concluded-red dispatched runs on the unchanged head from the head's own run list (a green run breaks the streak, a head move resets it by construction, cancelled is never a verdict) and at jobParams.redHeadParkCap (default 2) PARKS validation_failed with a report naming the failing job(s) + the failed-run link. The parked PR leaves validate-armed's FIFO (notLabels excludes it) — NO third dispatch. Machine PRs keep the rework arm (routing unchanged) and exit the park via the gh-750 machine self-clear / #633 RESET probes on the next head; guests keep the red-1 park. jobParams.redHeadParkCap=false disables the park (the 🔴 marker audit trail and the 3-red arm-side skip are untouched).",
sm_github.json:164:          "description": "Stale-arm sweeper (live: fa #999 — ai_validating held 7h with a CONCLUDED green CI and no verdict consumed; the ai_validating mutex stayed held forever. unarm-stale-validation covers BEHIND only). ai_validating + the head's dispatched validation run CONCLUDED (success or failure — CANCELLED is never a verdict) more than staleMinutes (15) ago, arm never consumed → unarm. Success side: unarm + re-latch ai_validated (complete_validation parity — the merge window re-flows; validate-armed latch-skips on the unchanged head). Failure side: the standard fail path (report + machine-only rework re-arm). Fresh conclusions (<15 min) never sweep: the check-visibility/verdict race window — the same-tick verdict rules (merge-validated / fail-validation / validated-green) own those. BEHIND excluded: unarm-stale-validation owns the moved-base recovery. gh-821 ZOMBIE side (live: fa #1443, 2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z — the dispatched run concluded CANCELLED in the gh-748 kicker/dispatch race, this sweep kept the arm ('no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays') and four validated PRs deferred on the ai_validating mutex for ~2h until a manual gh workflow run ci.yml): a CANCELLED-only head or a head with NO dispatched run at all is a ZOMBIE — the arm holds the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it. Past the 15-min visibility grace (probe.active still reads 'running' inside it, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes) the liveness classification (js/common/validationLiveness.js) re-dispatches validation the SAME TICK — release the slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (a LIVE run now backs the mutex; no parallel validations) — logging '🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N'. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour (jobParams.zombieRedispatchMinMs, default 3600000), bookkept as marker comments (🔄 zombie re-dispatch <sha> — zombie N/cap at <iso>, the red-head carrier); 3 re-dispatches in a row on the same head (jobParams.zombieRedispatchCap, default 3) park validation_failed + explanatory comment — fail-closed, a new push (new head SHA) restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes. A live run keeps the arm exactly as before (AC3 — healthy flow untouched).",
sm_github.json:182:          "description": "Every open non-draft PR behind main gets a silent branch refresh with the workflow token (pushes trigger no workflows, so freshness is free); validating PRs are excluded so the validation head never moves mid-run. mergeState is BEHIND only: the prStatus deterministic override computes BEHIND from base freshness (immune to the REST BEHIND/BLOCKED flip-flop this rule used to paper over with both values), and BLOCKED is now a REAL verdict (fresh head, required checks pending/red) — updating those would no-op-clone every pending PR on every tick. Limit 20 (owner 2026-09-22): silent pushes fire no CI — refreshing every BEHIND head every tick is free and keeps PRs merge-ready, so the merge window never waits for a refresh first. STICKY PARK (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923): before refreshing, a GUEST PR whose current head has RED checks is labeled validation_failed (idempotent, the head SHA noted in a one-time comment) — validate-armed excludes the label and no validation CI is dispatched for it at all; the label is REMOVED only when the LAST SUBSTANTIVE commit (machine-authored merges of main walked back past, dmtools-agents#681) is a NON-machine push NEWER than the park, so the SM's own silent-updates — bot merges or re-arms — never clear a red guest's park. Machine-authored PRs never get the label (fa pushes their heads; the label's SET rules are guest-gated — legacy parks predate that). MACHINE SELF-CLEAR (gh-750, owner directive 2026-10-05): a MACHINE-authored parked PR — legacy residue like fa#1227, the label predates this guest-only contract — clears when the current head's check rollup is GREEN or the head moved past the park carrying no red verdict of its own (probe failures keep the park, fail closed); guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior.",
sm_github.json:199:          "description": "Sticky-park RESET for NON-BEHIND heads (dmtools-agents, live fa 2026-10-03): the human-push unpark probe lives inside update_branch, but silent-update-behind only matches mergeState BEHIND — a guest PR whose fix commit lands on the SAME base (not behind) NEVER runs the RESET and the park outlives any human push (live: vendor pushed 16:01 to five parked approved PRs; 2h later not one label cleared, the whole approved FIFO frozen). This rule routes every parked non-validating PR through update_branch's RESET probe regardless of merge state: a NON-machine SUBSTANTIVE push NEWER than the newest park event clears the label — the probe walks back past machine-authored merges of main to the last substantive commit: a bot merge BURIES the retrigger, never replaces it (dmtools-agents#681, live fa#1213 2026-10-03 22:56–23:10: retrigger 7ecf11d7 buried by bot merge b3f9c6b5 before the next tick, the old head-keyed probe declined and the park survived 4 real ticks); then validate-armed picks the PR up on a later pass (this rule never dispatches CI itself); machine pushes and stale heads keep the park (fail closed). The silent branch refresh inside the action is a no-op for a non-BEHIND head (git merge reports up-to-date, no push). MACHINE SELF-CLEAR (gh-750, owner directive 2026-10-05, live fa#1227): this rule is a MACHINE-authored parked PR's only exit when the head is NOT BEHIND (silent-update-behind serves BEHIND heads through the same shared RESET probe) — fa pushes their own heads, so the non-machine substantive push never lands, the #633 park-comment sha is missing on legacy parks, and the rework armers list validation_failed as an in-flight blocker so no rework leg fires (#1227: pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + MERGEABLE, parked since the CI-storm era). BEHIND/DIRTY excluded like validate-armed. MUTEX with mutexExcludeSelf (multi-arm leak fix, live: fa 2026-09-26 — 7 approved PRs held ai_validating simultaneously: 922/923/930/932/934/948/961, +1 arm per tick): this rule previously ran with NO mutex because the global mutex scan sees the rule's own armed target and self-blocks 100% of the time — and its 'structural serialization' assumption (validate-armed's mutex guarantees <=1 armed approved PR) is FALSE once heads move: silent-update / BEHIND unarm races / guest pushes keep feeding checks=none states, and each tick this rule armed one more approved PR. # gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

AC2: runner cost reported per tick (validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
Test plan L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).

So the design:
1. Add a `mutexMax` (or `maxHolders`) option to the mutex logic in githubSource.js — allow up to N holders of the mutex within mutexAmong scope.
2. The knob: repo var or jobParams, e.g. `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1). Maybe a watermark: flip to 2/3 when approved queue exceeds a watermark — e.g. `validationConcurrencyWatermark`.
3. Update the action-time mutex re-check in smAgent.js (`validationMutexHeldByAnother`) to allow N concurrent arms.
4. Runner cost reporting per tick (AC2): report validation-minutes per tick in the tick log.
5. Unit tests in js/unit-tests/.

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

content.text:
/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge.
AC2: runner cost reported per tick (validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
Test plan L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).

So the design:
1. Add a `mutexMax` (or `maxHolders`) option to the mutex logic in githubSource.js — allow up to N holders of the mutex within mutexAmong scope.

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

blocks.text:
Now I understand the structure. The task (gh-837) asks: implement parallel validations (N=2-3) by relaxing mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations, with a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.

AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge.
AC2: runner cost reported per tick (validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
Test plan L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).

So the design:
1. Add a `mutexMax` (or `maxHolders`) option to the mutex logic in githubSource.js — allow up to N holders of the mutex within mutexAmong scope.
2. The knob: repo var or jobParams, e.g. `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1). Maybe a watermark: flip to 2/3 when approved queue exceeds a watermark — e.g. `validationConcurrencyWatermark`.
3. Update the action-time mutex re-check in smAgent.js (`validationMutexHeldByAnother`) to allow N concurrent arms.
4. Runner cost reporting per tick (AC2): report validation-minutes per tick in the tick log.
5. Unit tests in js/unit-tests/.

Let me look at the unit tests to understand test patterns, and how jobParams are plumbed into githubSource query. Also check smProvider / how query gets to githubSource — the mutex evaluation happens in githubSource (queryPrs?), and the knob would be a query-level parameter like `mutexMax`.

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that

 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).
