/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).

 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).

 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration

 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

blocks.text:
Now I understand the structure. The task (gh-837) asks: implement parallel validations (N=2-3) by relaxing mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations, with a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.

AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge.
AC2: runner cost reported per tick (validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
Test plan L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).

So the design:

/**

 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget)."

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

Now I understand the structure. The task (gh-837) asks: implement parallel validations (N=2-3) by relaxing mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations, with a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.

AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge.
AC2: runner cost reported per tick (validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
Test plan L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).

So the design:
1. Add a `mutexMax` (or `maxHolders`) option to the mutex logic in githubSource.js — allow up to N holders of the mutex within mutexAmong scope.
2. The knob: repo var or jobParams, e.g. `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1). Maybe a watermark: flip to 2/3 when approved queue exceeds a watermark — e.g. `validationConcurrencyWatermark`.
3. Update the action-time mutex re-check in smAgent.js (`validationMutexHeldByAnother`) to allow N concurrent arms.
4. Runner cost reporting per tick (AC2): report validation-minutes per tick in the tick log.
5. Unit tests in js/unit-tests/.

Let me look at the unit tests to understand test patterns, and how jobParams are plumbed into githubSource query. Also check smProvider / how query gets to githubSource — the mutex evaluation happens in githubSource (queryPrs?), and the knob would be a query-level parameter like `mutexMax`.

Where's the approved queue depth known? In smAgent where jobParams available. The query object could carry `mutexMax: N`.

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.

 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly

{
  "key": "gh-837",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed",
    "description": "## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget)."
  }
}

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).

 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering
